When I checked, all four were in fact correct.Like (3)ReplyShareBruce J Jones6dIt seems like alot of people are stressed out now. That is entirely appropriate. We all happen to be alive during the greatest crisis humanity has ever faced and if that doesn't cause a little stress then you are not paying attention. Politically and economically we are in a conflict between declining and ascending nations; U.S. and China. Environmentally human activity has bumped the climate into a hotter more extreme mode which will ultimately lead to food shortages. The stress a massive human population on Earth's support system is a factor that is often ignored. The introduction of impacts human technology would involve a long list that would include toxicity and AI.Each nation has its own stress factors. For example India has a massive population and the U.S. has a burdensome old population (baby boomers). So taken all together there is a compelling argument that humanity is facing its greatest crisis ever.In the past the plagues or famine or war occured in a region while in other other parts of the planet there could be a golden era. Due to our high population combined with high technology the scope of the crisis is global. Consequenty the scope of the solution is also global. A useful mental model would be that we humans have accidently turned a natural life supporting planet into a poorly run spacestation. Report to your duty stations!Like (3)ReplyShareJeri6dThese guys know way, way more than I do, obviously, but it just seems too simplistic to think that Anthropic or OpenAI could take over as much of the global economy as they want with their models with the end goal of being Claude's project. The ecosystem is not in their control at this point. It needs Google, Intel, NVIDIA, TSMC, ASML, among many others to run their software.
